label: prf:sl2-prolongation-recurrence
title: Proof of the symplectic one-parameter recurrence
html:
Proof. Proof of the symplectic one-parameter recurrence

By prop:prolonged-periods-fixed-depth the prolongation acts through a 2\times 2 operator B on the W-Hodge plane, and Cayley--Hamilton gives B^2 = \mathrm{tr}(B)\,B - \det(B)\,\mathbf 1.

The cup-product pairing \langle\alpha,\beta\rangle = \int \alpha\wedge\beta on H^1 is a symplectic form preserved by the Gauss--Manin monodromy (it is topological, hence flat for \nabla). It is S_5-invariant and restricts non-degenerately to the rank-2 W-isotypic Hodge plane (the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations make \langle H^{1,0}, H^{0,1}\rangle a perfect pairing). Therefore B preserves a non-degenerate alternating form on a 2-dimensional space, i.e. B \in \mathrm{Sp}(2) = \mathrm{SL}_2, so \det B = 1.

Substituting \det B = 1 into Cayley--Hamilton gives B^2 = \tau\,B - \mathbf 1 with \tau = \mathrm{tr}\, B. Multiplying by B^n and using B^{n}\!\cdot B^2 = B^{n+2}, B^{n}\!\cdot B = B^{n+1},

B^{\,n+2} = B^n(\tau B - \mathbf 1) = \tau\,B^{\,n+1} - B^{\,n},

which is the Lean theorem QOU.Mass.sl2_prolongation_recurrence (rw [pow_add, hCH, mul_sub, mul_one, mul_smul_comm, ← pow_succ]). Applying the period functional \varphi(\,\cdot\,v_0) gives a_D^{(n+2)} = \tau\,a_D^{(n+1)} - a_D^{(n)}, leaving the single unknown \tau, recoverable from any three consecutive periods as \tau = (a_D^{(n)} + a_D^{(n+2)})/a_D^{(n+1)}. \qquad\blacksquare
